The Festive Round-Neck Raglan

I knitted this red-and-green jumper from the top down, with a shaped round neck, tapered sleeves and simple ribbed edges. Here’s the stitch-by-stitch plan I used to make it.

Before you cast on

Use Aran yarn and 6 mm (US 10) circular needles, or the needle size that gives you 13 stitches and 18 rows per 10 cm in blocked stockinette. You’ll also need four raglan markers, a distinct beginning-of-round marker, waste yarn or holders, a tapestry needle and a way to knit small circumferences.

Swatch in stockinette and check your gauge after washing and drying. Compare the calculated sizes below with a jumper you like the fit of. I entered a 90 cm chest with 10 cm of ease, and a 28 cm upper arm with 4 cm of ease.

MeasurementTargetCalculated
Chest circumference100 cm98.46 cm
Upper-arm circumference32 cm32.31 cm
Yoke shaping depth, excluding neckband20 cm20 cm (36 shaping rows and rounds)
Underarm to hem, including ribbing40 cmAbout 40 cm
Underarm to cuff, including ribbing43 cmAbout 42.8 cm
Cuff circumference at stockinette gauge20 cm20 cm before ribbing draws in
Neckband depth3 cmAbout 2.8 cm (5 rounds)
Hem and cuff ribbing depth5 cm eachAbout 5 cm each (9 rounds)

The calculator used a 50 cm base neck input for stitch allocation and calculated a 49.23 cm base opening. Check the shaped neckline and finished ribbing for fit. Each 6-stitch underarm bridge is about 4.62 cm at gauge.

The calculated dimensions use the stated gauge. Measure the ribbing as you go for precise lengths. Yarn brand and meterage for the sample are unconfirmed.

Knit the yoke

Cast on and shape the neckline flat

Cast on 46 stitches without ribbing. Place a marker at each dash in this order: front 2 — sleeve 10 — back 22 — sleeve 10 — front 2. Start shaping on row 1 (right side). Turn at the end of every flat row and purl the even-numbered wrong-side rows.

The first 10 rows lower the front opening by about 5.6 cm from the back cast-on level before ribbing. On the right-side rows below, add the listed number of stitches at each front edge as well as working the raglan increases. Cable cast on at the start and use backward loops at the end.

RowCast on at each front edgeRaglan increases
10Body and sleeves
31Body only
50Body and sleeves
72Body and sleeves
91Body only

After row 10: 32 back stitches, 11 on each front and 16 on each sleeve (86 stitches total).

Join at centre front on row 11

With the right side facing, cable cast on 10 stitches at the start of row 11. Knit the new stitches, then work across the existing stitches with both body and sleeve increases. At the end of the row, check that the work is untwisted, place a distinct beginning-of-round marker immediately before the first new stitch, and join by knitting that stitch to begin round 12. Row 11 counts once. The centre-front marker marks the round boundary. The four original markers mark the increase points.

Work the body and sleeve increases

  • Body: Every odd row or round from 1 through 35, add one stitch at each raglan edge of the front and back (+4).
  • Sleeves: On rows or rounds 1, 5, 7, 11, 13, 15, 19, 21, 23, 27, 29, 33 and 35, add one stitch at each raglan edge of both sleeves (+4).

At each raglan marker, work to one stitch before it. M1L if the section before the marker is due an increase, knit one, slip the marker, knit one, then M1R if the section after the marker is due an increase. When both sections are scheduled, work both increases. If a front section has only one stitch and the increase would fall at the edge without a strand to lift, substitute one backward-loop increase at the edge.

After joining, knit all even rounds plain. Once you finish round 36, try on the yoke and check that you have 58 front, 58 back and 36 stitches for each sleeve (188 total).

Divide and knit the body

Work the front and back stitches in the round. Slip each set of 36 sleeve stitches onto a holder as you reach it and cast on 6 stitches in its place. You’ll have 128 body stitches including the two underarm bridges.

After the division, knit 63 plain rounds, then work 9 rounds of knit-one, purl-one rib. Bind off elastically.

Knit the tapered sleeves

For each sleeve, return the 36 held stitches to the needles and pick up 6 stitches across the underarm. Place the beginning-of-round marker at the centre of the underarm. If you pick up extra corner stitches to close gaps, decrease those back to 42 stitches before beginning the schedule.

Starting at the underarm, knit 68 rounds in total. On rounds 9, 17, 26, 34, 43, 51, 60 and 68, work k1, k2tog, knit to the last 3 stitches, ssk, k1. Knit the remaining rounds plain. You’ll end with 26 stitches (20 cm at stockinette gauge before the ribbing draws in).

Work 9 rounds of knit-one, purl-one rib, then bind off elastically. Repeat for the second sleeve and check length before binding off.

Pick up the neckband and finish

With the right side facing, pick up 22 stitches across the original back cast-on edge, 10 across each sleeve cast-on edge, 10 across the centre-front bridge and about 8 along each shaped front edge (including the two original front cast-on stitches per side). Aim for about 68 stitches. Adjust the spacing so the band lies flat and keep the total even.

Join and work 5 rounds of knit-one, purl-one rib. Bind off elastically and check that the opening passes comfortably over your head. Weave in the ends and block gently according to the yarn’s care instructions.

Knitting terms

M1L: Lift the strand between the needles from front to back and knit through its back loop.

M1R: Lift it from back to front and knit through its front loop.

k2tog: Knit two stitches together.

ssk: Slip two stitches knitwise one at a time, then knit them together through the back loops.

Stockinette: Knit the right-side rows and purl the wrong-side rows when flat. In the round, knit every round.

Decorate your Christmas jumper

Once your jumper is finished and dry, lay it flat and try a few arrangements before sewing anything on. Use these two photos for ideas and place the decorations wherever you like them best.

For a wearable version, tack the felt shapes down with a few small stitches and sew any bells and pom-poms on securely. Leave the neckline, cuffs and hem clear so the ribbing can stretch. Use the fairy lights as a photo prop and remove them before wearing or washing the jumper.
